title: dllexport or dllimport
description:
The export macro in a DLL's public header expands to one thing while the DLL itself is being built and another everywhere else. Write

```cpp
std::string apiMacroFor(bool buildingTheDll);
```

that returns the text the macro should expand to: `"__declspec(dllexport)"` while building the DLL, `"__declspec(dllimport)"` for any program that uses it.

Then write `std::string exportsSymbol(const std::string& projectName)`: the preprocessor symbol Visual Studio's DLL template defines for a project, which is the project name in upper case followed by `_EXPORTS`. Only letters and digits are kept; anything else becomes `_`.

```
exportsSymbol("StoneMath") == "STONEMATH_EXPORTS"
exportsSymbol("my-lib 2") == "MY_LIB_2_EXPORTS"
```
lessonTitle: Your First DLL in Visual Studio
